block.txt: An Act to establish authorities to manage sporting venues for the State and specific regions of the State; and for other purposes.
This Act is the Sporting Venues Authorities Act 2008.
This Act commences on a day or days to be appointed by proclamation.
In this Act—
advisory committee means a committee established under section 21C and includes a membership advisory committee.

assets means any legal or equitable estate or interest (whether present or future, whether vested or contingent and whether personal or assignable) in real or personal property of any description (including money), and includes securities, choses in action and documents.
authority’s land means, in relation to a sporting venues authority, land vested in or managed by that authority.
Board of Venues NSW means the Board of Venues NSW provided by section 15.
Chief Executive Officer means the Chief Executive Officer of Venues NSW.
controlled land means the lands described in Schedule 4A, Part 3.
designated land means the land described in Schedule 4A, Part 2.
function includes a power, authority or duty, and exercise a function includes perform a duty.
government agency means—
a public authority constituted by or under an Act, or
a NSW Government agency, or
a Division of the Government Service, or
a local authority, or
a State owned corporation.
liabilities means any liabilities, debts or obligations (whether present or future, whether vested or contingent and whether personal or assignable).
membership advisory committee means a membership advisory committee established by section 21E.
private corporation means a corporation within the meaning of the Corporations Act 2001 of the Commonwealth formed in or outside New South Wales.
private subsidiary corporation means a private corporation in which a sporting venues authority has a controlling interest.
ranger means a person appointed under section 37 to be a ranger.
rights means any rights, powers, privileges or immunities (whether present or future, whether vested or contingent and whether personal or assignable).
scheduled lands means the land described in Schedule 4A, Part 1.
sporting venues authority means the State Sporting Venues Authority or Venues NSW.
State Sporting Venues Authority means the State Sporting Venues Authority constituted under this Act.
Venues NSW means Venues NSW constituted by this Act.
Venues NSW’s land means the land vested in or managed by Venues NSW and includes land described in Schedule 4A.
The Interpretation Act 1987 contains definitions and other provisions that affect the interpretation and application of this Act.
Notes included in this Act do not form part of this Act.
The objects of this Act are as follows—
to enable the efficient and effective management and coordination of entertainment and sporting venues within the State on a commercial basis,
to attract and encourage the holding of major events at entertainment and sporting venues within the State,
to facilitate the development of precincts surrounding the entertainment and sporting venues that Venues NSW owns or operates,

to ensure a customer-focused approach is applied to the management of entertainment and sporting venues and surrounding lands so they remain accessible to, and meet the needs of, users of and visitors to the venues and the broader community,
to ensure the provision of entertainment and sporting venues fulfils community service obligations that may be determined by the Minister from time to time.

heading.b: Constitution and administration of State Sporting Venues Authority
Constitution of State Sporting Venues Authority

block.txt: There is constituted by this Act a corporation with the corporate name of State Sporting Venues Authority.

heading.b: Status of State Sporting Venues Authority

block.txt: The State Sporting Venues Authority is a NSW Government agency.
The Minister is responsible for the day-to-day management of the affairs of the State Sporting Venues Authority.
Any act, matter or thing done in the name of, or on behalf of, the State Sporting Venues Authority by the Minister is taken to have been done by the Authority.

heading.b: Delegation of State Sporting Venues Authority’s functions

block.txt: The State Sporting Venues Authority may delegate to an authorised person any of its functions, other than this power of delegation.
A delegate may sub-delegate to an authorised person any function delegated by the State Sporting Venues Authority if the delegate is authorised in writing to do so by the Authority.
In this section, authorised person means—
a member of staff of the State Sporting Venues Authority, or
a government agency or member of staff of a government agency.

heading.b: Functions of State Sporting Venues Authority
Functions of State Sporting Venues Authority

block.txt: The principal functions of the State Sporting Venues Authority are as follows—
to maintain and improve the authority’s land,
to establish and manage sporting grounds, sporting facilities and recreational facilities (whether or not on the authority’s land),
to establish and manage facilities for the purposes of sporting competitions, sports training and sports education (whether or not on the authority’s land),
to establish and manage community facilities and to establish and manage facilities for community and recreational purposes (whether or not on the authority’s land),

to permit the use of the whole or any part of the authority’s land for activities of a sporting, recreational or community nature, including the use of that land for events and general community access,
to encourage the use and enjoyment of the authority’s land by the public and clubs, associations or other bodies, where appropriate in its opinion,
to undertake or provide, or facilitate the undertaking or provision of, commercial and retail activities and facilities on the authority’s land,
to make all reasonable attempts to ensure that any new development carried out on the authority’s land accords with best practice environmental and planning standards,
to ensure that proper asset management plans are in place and are implemented for the authority’s land.

The State Sporting Venues Authority may enter into an arrangement with Venues NSW for Venues NSW to manage any land vested in the State Sporting Venues Authority and to perform any function that the State Sporting Venues Authority has in relation to that land.

The State Sporting Venues Authority may do all such supplemental, incidental or consequential acts as may be necessary or expedient for the exercise of its functions, including entering into any contract or arrangement with any person in connection with the carrying out of its functions.
Persons may be employed in the Public Service under the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 to enable the State Sporting Venues Authority to exercise its functions.

Section 59 of the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 provides that the persons so employed (or whose services the State Sporting Venues Authority makes use of) may be referred to as officers or employees, or members of staff, of the State Sporting Venues Authority. Section 47A of the Constitution Act 1902 precludes the State Sporting Venues Authority from employing staff.
The State Sporting Venues Authority has such other functions as are conferred or imposed on it by or under this or any other Act.

heading.b: Exercise of functions through private subsidiaries, joint ventures etc

block.txt: Any function of the State Sporting Venues Authority may be exercised—
by the Authority itself, or
by a private subsidiary corporation, or
by the Authority or such a private subsidiary corporation, or both, in a partnership, joint venture or other association with other persons or bodies.
The State Sporting Venues Authority may—
form, or participate in the formation of, private corporations, and
acquire interests in private corporations, and
sell or otherwise dispose of interests in private corporations.
A private subsidiary corporation is not, and does not represent, the Crown.

heading.b: Constitution and administration of Venues NSW

block.txt: There is constituted by this Act a corporation with the corporate name of Venues NSW.
Venues NSW is a NSW Government agency.
Venues NSW is subject to the control and direction of the Minister in the exercise of its functions.
There is to be a Board of Venues NSW.
The Board of Venues NSW is to consist of the following members appointed by the Minister—
1 person appointed by the Minister as the Chairperson of the Board,
1 person appointed by the Minister as the Deputy Chairperson of the Board,
1 person who is a Public Service senior executive within the meaning of the Government Sector Employment Act 2013,
1 person who resides in the Hunter Region,
1 person who resides in the Wollongong Region,
at least 6, but not more than 8, other persons.

The Board of Venues NSW is responsible for the major sporting facilities in NSW and in particular, the unique heritage and historical role of the Sydney Cricket Ground (since 1854), Sydney Cricket Ground Trust (since 1875) and Sydney Cricket and Sports Ground Trust (since 1952) in the sporting and civic life of the State, when, at various times, the SCG has been the primary home of—
Cricket: Inter-colonial, Test Match, Sheffield Shield and limited-over international and domestic;
Rugby League;
Rugby Union;
Soccer/Football;
Australian Football;
Cycling;
Baseball; and
Athletics, hosting the 1938 Empire Games.

And home to military recruitment and barracks during World Wars One and Two; also served as the principal location for the 1901 Australian Federation celebrations; and through the work of the SCG Trust, contributed heavily to charitable and civic-minded causes in NSW.
Schedule 1 sets out provisions relating to the members and procedure of the Board of Venues NSW.

heading.b: Chief Executive Officer of Venues NSW

block.txt: The Minister may, in consultation with the Board of Venues NSW, appoint a Chief Executive Officer of Venues NSW.
The Chief Executive Officer is responsible for the day-to-day management of the affairs of Venues NSW in accordance with the policies and general directions of the Board of Venues NSW.
Any act, matter or thing done in the name of, or on behalf of, Venues NSW by the Chief Executive Officer is taken to have been done by Venues NSW.
The Chief Executive Officer may attend, and participate in discussions at, meetings of the Board of Venues NSW unless otherwise directed by the Board, but is not entitled to vote at the meetings.
Schedule 2 sets out further provisions relating to the Chief Executive Officer.
Persons may be employed in the Public Service under the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 to enable Venues NSW to exercise its functions.

Section 59 of the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 provides that the persons so employed (or whose services Venues NSW makes use of) may be referred to as officers or employees, or members of staff, of Venues NSW. Section 47A of the Constitution Act 1902 precludes Venues NSW from employing staff.

heading.b: Holder of office not affected by appointment to Venues NSW or its Board

block.txt: The doctrine of incompatibility of office—

does not operate to prevent the holder of a position in a government sector agency (the original position) from being appointed to a position in Venues NSW or on its Board (the additional position), and
does not operate to effect or require the holder of the original position to surrender or vacate the position as a result of the appointment to the additional position.
This section applies even if the original position or the additional position is held on an acting or temporary basis.
This section does not limit section 73 of the Government Sector Employment Act 2013.
In this section—
government sector agency has the same meaning as in the Government Sector Employment Act 2013.
The principal functions of Venues NSW are as follows—

to provide advice to the Minister on the State’s entertainment and sporting venues management strategy and development of existing or new entertainment and sporting venues and their surrounding precincts,
to maintain and improve Venues NSW’s land,
to establish, manage and improve sporting grounds, events grounds and associated facilities for the purposes of sports, events and recreation,
to establish, manage and improve facilities for the purposes of sporting competitions, sports training and sports education,
to establish, manage and improve community facilities and to establish, manage and improve facilities for community and recreational purposes,
to permit the use of the whole or any part of Venues NSW’s land for activities of a sporting, recreational or community nature, including the use of the land for events and general community access,
to encourage, if Venues NSW considers it appropriate, the use and enjoyment of Venues NSW’s land by the public and clubs, associations or other bodies,
to collaborate with public sector agencies and other bodies to promote the use of Venues NSW’s land and facilities for commercial purposes,
to undertake or provide, or facilitate the undertaking or provision of, commercial and retail activities and facilities on Venues NSW’s land,
to make all reasonable attempts to ensure new development carried out on Venues NSW’s land accords with environmental and planning laws, standards and best practice,
to contribute to proposals for the design, development and management of land neighbouring Venues NSW’s land,
to meet the community service obligations determined from time to time by the Minister in relation to the provision of entertainment and sporting venues.

Venues NSW may undertake supplemental, incidental or consequential acts as may be necessary or expedient for the exercise of its functions, including entering into any contract or arrangement with any person in connection with the carrying out of its functions.
Venues NSW has other functions conferred or imposed on it by or under this Act or any other Act.
Venues NSW may delegate to an authorised person any of its functions, other than this power of delegation.
A delegate may sub-delegate to an authorised person any function delegated by Venues NSW if the delegate is authorised in writing to do so by Venues NSW.
In this section, authorised person means—
a member of staff of Venues NSW, or
a government agency or member of staff of a government agency, or
an advisory committee or member of an advisory committee.
Venues NSW may—
form, or participate in the formation of, private corporations, and
acquire interests in private corporations, and
sell or otherwise dispose of interests in private corporations.
A private subsidiary corporation is not, and does not represent, the Crown.

heading.b: Exercise of functions through private subsidiary corporations or with other persons or bodies

block.txt: A function of Venues NSW may be exercised—
by Venues NSW itself, or
by a private subsidiary corporation, or
by Venues NSW or a private subsidiary corporation, or both, in a partnership, joint venture or other association with other persons or bodies.
In this Part—
commencement day means the day on which this Part commences.
done includes omitted to be done.
liability means civil liability and includes action, claim and demand.
Venues NSW may establish advisory committees to—
provide advice to the Minister or to Venues NSW, or
enable Venues NSW to exercise its functions.
Subject to any directions given by the Minister, the procedure of an advisory committee is to be determined by the Board of Venues NSW.
A member of an advisory committee is an honorary member and no remuneration is payable to the member in respect of the duties they perform as a member of the advisory committee.
An advisory committee, other than a membership advisory committee, may be dissolved or merged with another advisory committee at any time.
The regulations may provide for the following—
the establishment and functions of an advisory committee,
the membership of an advisory committee,
the procedure and dissolution of an advisory committee,
the appointment, term of office and removal from office of members of an advisory committee.

Venues NSW must, within 6 months of the commencement day, establish an advisory committee in respect of each of the following regions to provide advice to the Minister and to Venues NSW regarding the entertainment and sporting venues and their surrounding precincts in those regions—
the Hunter Region,
the Wollongong Region.
The following membership advisory committees are established on the commencement day—

a committee to provide advice to Venues NSW regarding the membership of persons who were formerly Members of the Sydney Cricket Ground, as referred to in clause 37 of the Sydney Cricket Ground and Sydney Football Stadium By-law 2014 before its repeal,
a committee to provide advice to Venues NSW regarding the membership of persons who were given membership to stadia vested in Venues NSW before the commencement day.
Venues NSW is to ensure a former member is invited to become a member of—
if the former member was a member of the Sydney Cricket and Sports Ground Trust—the membership advisory committee established under subsection (1)(a), or
if the former member was a member of the former board of management of Venues NSW—the membership advisory committee established under subsection (1)(b).
A person becomes a member of a membership advisory committee—
if the person is a former member—
on the day the former member accepts Venues NSW’s invitation to become a member of the membership advisory committee, and
in accordance with subsection (2), or
if the person who is elected, in accordance with Schedule 3, as a member of the membership advisory committee established under subsection (1)(a)—on the date of the person’s election.
A membership advisory committee may be dissolved or merged with another advisory committee on the expiration of the remainder of the terms of office of—

for a membership advisory committee established under subsection (1)(a)—all of the former members of the Sydney Cricket and Sports Ground Trust who have been appointed as members of the membership advisory committee, or

for a membership advisory committee established under subsection (1)(b)—all of the former members of the former board of management of Venues NSW who have been appointed as members of the membership advisory committee.
A member of a membership advisory committee is not personally subject to any liability for anything done—
in good faith, and
for the purpose of executing functions under this Act.
The liability instead attaches to the Crown.
In this section—
former board of management of Venues NSW means the board of management of Venues NSW before Venues NSW was reconstituted by Schedule 5, Part 6.
former member means a person who—
was, immediately before its dissolution, a member of—
the Sydney Cricket and Sports Ground Trust, or
the former board of management of Venues NSW, and
is not appointed as a member of the Board of Venues NSW.

heading.b: Advisory Committee: Sydney Cricket Ground Heritage

block.txt: Venues NSW must, within 6 months of the commencement day, establish a body to be known as the ‘SCG Heritage Trust’, advising the Minister and Venues NSW on—
The preservation and public promotion of the unique sporting and civic history of the SCG;
Proposed changes in the design, amenity and management of the SCG that may affect its heritage values;
Harnessing the skills and interests of historians and sporting enthusiasts to further develop the historical record and status of the SCG; and
The custodianship of the highly significant historical role and contribution of the SCG Trust.
Members of this advisory committee must be appointed on the basis of their well-established and meritorious sporting, administrative or research/published association with the ground.

heading.b: Provisions relating to vesting of and dealings with land and other property
Vesting of land in sporting venues authorities

block.txt: In this Division—
land of a government agency means—
land that is vested in the government agency, or land that is vested in the Crown or Her Majesty and that is controlled and used by the government agency, or
an interest in land, being an interest that is vested in or held by the government agency.
relevant authority means, in relation to land described in Schedule 4, the sporting venues authority specified opposite the land in that Schedule.
transfer date means—

in relation to land included in Schedule 4 by order under section 24—the date of publication of the order on the NSW legislation website or a later date specified in the order in respect of the land, or
in relation to land included in Schedule 4 by an amendment made by an Act—the date on which the amendment takes effect.
transferor, in relation to land included in Schedule 4, means the person or body in whom or which the land was vested immediately before the transfer date.

heading.b: Transfer of property to sporting venues authorities

block.txt: On the transfer date relating to land included in Schedule 4, the land vests in the relevant authority for an estate in fee simple (or such other interest as is specified in the Schedule)—
without the need for any further conveyance, transfer, assignment or assurance, and
subject to any trusts, estates, interests, dedications, conditions, restrictions and covenants to which the land was subject immediately before the transfer date.
On the transfer date relating to land included in Schedule 4, the following provisions have effect—
the rights or liabilities of the transferor in relation to the land become by virtue of this section the rights or liabilities of the relevant authority,

all proceedings relating to the land commenced before the transfer date by or on behalf of, or against, the transferor or a predecessor of the transferor and pending immediately before the transfer date are taken to be proceedings pending by or against the relevant authority,

any act, matter or thing done or omitted to be done in relation to the land before the transfer date by, to or in respect of the transferor is (to the extent to which that act, matter or thing has any force or effect) taken to have been done or omitted by, to or in respect of the relevant authority,

a reference in any Act, in any instrument made under any Act or in any document of any kind to the transferor or a predecessor of the transferor is (to the extent that it relates to that land or those rights or liabilities but subject to the regulations), to be read as, or as including, a reference to the relevant authority.

Regulations may be made for or with respect to the conversion of references to the transferor in any document or class of documents to references to the relevant authority as a consequence of any transfer of land under this Division.

heading.b: Transfer of additional property to authority—amendment of Schedule 4

block.txt: The Governor may, by order published on the NSW legislation website—
amend Schedule 4 by inserting, altering or omitting the name of a sporting venues authority or a description of land, or
substitute Schedule 4.
Land is authorised to be included in Schedule 4 by order under this section only if—
it is land of a government agency (including vacant Crown land), and
the appropriate consent has been obtained to the land being included in the order.
For the purposes of subsection (2), the appropriate consent is—
where the government agency concerned is not a local authority—the consent of the Minister responsible for the government agency, or
where the government agency concerned is a local authority—the consent of the local authority.

Subject to section 23 (1) (b), this section does not prevent land, the fee simple in which is vested in Her Majesty, the Crown or a government agency, or vacant Crown land, from being transferred by order under this section even if the land is subject to other interests.

Subject to the other provisions of this section, land may be transferred by order under this section despite any requirement of any other Act or law that relates to dealing with or disposing of the land.

heading.b: Effect of transfer of land under this Division

block.txt: No compensation is payable to any person or body in connection with the operation of this Division.
The operation of this Division is not to be regarded—
as a breach of contract or confidence or otherwise as a civil wrong, or
as a breach of any contractual provision prohibiting, restricting or regulating the assignment or transfer of assets, rights or liabilities, or

as giving rise to any remedy by a party to an instrument, or as causing or permitting the termination of any instrument, because of a change in the beneficial or legal ownership of any asset, right or liability.
The operation of this Division is not to be regarded as an event of default under any contract or other instrument.
No attornment to the transferee by a lessee from a transferor is required.

heading.b: Competition authorisations relating to transfer of land under this Division

block.txt: Conduct authorised or required by or under the provisions of this Division is specifically authorised by this Act for the purposes of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 of the Commonwealth and the Competition Code of New South Wales.

Conduct authorised by this section is authorised only to the extent (if any) it would otherwise contravene Part IV of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 of the Commonwealth and the Competition Code of New South Wales.
A sporting venues authority may sell, lease, exchange or otherwise dispose of or deal with any land vested in the authority and grant easements or rights-of-way over such land or any part of it.
Venues NSW may take action under subsection (1) only with the consent of the Minister.

heading.b: Acquisition of property by gift, devise or bequest

block.txt: A sporting venues authority may acquire by gift, devise or bequest any property for the purposes of this Act and may agree to carry out the conditions of any such gift, devise or bequest.
The rule of law against remoteness of vesting does not apply to any condition of a gift, devise or bequest to which the sporting venues authority has agreed.
The Duties Act 1997 does not apply to or in respect of any gift, devise or bequest made or to be made to a sporting venues authority.

heading.b: Dealings with certain property that is held by sporting venues authority subject to a condition

block.txt: If property is held by a sporting venues authority subject to a condition to which the authority has agreed under section 27, the authority is not to dispose of or otherwise deal with any of the property except in accordance with the condition or in accordance with subsection (2).

If the authority resolves that any property held by the authority subject to such a condition is no longer required for the purposes of the authority or can no longer be used for those purposes, the authority may, despite that condition—
sell the property and retain the proceeds of sale as property of the authority, or
exchange the property for other property that is capable of being used for the purposes of the authority, or
give the property to an institution that engages in activities of a sporting, recreational, educational or cultural nature, or
if the authority is of the opinion that the property is of no commercial value—dispose of or otherwise deal with the property without valuable consideration.

Venues NSW is not to sell, exchange, give, dispose of or otherwise deal with property under this section except with the consent of the Minister and in accordance with any condition that the Minister may impose on the grant of that consent.

The Minister may consent to the sale, exchange, gift or disposal of, or to any other dealing with, property for the purposes of this section and may impose any condition that the Minister thinks fit on the grant of that consent.

The State Sporting Venues Authority may acquire land or any interest in land, for the purposes of this Act, by agreement or by compulsory process in accordance with the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991.
Venues NSW may acquire land or any interest in land, for the purposes of this Act, by agreement.

For the purposes of the Public Works Act 1912, any acquisition of land under this Act is taken to be an authorised work, and the sporting venues authority that acquired the land is, in relation to that authorised work, taken to be the Constructing Authority.
Sections 34, 35, 36 and 37 of the Public Works Act 1912 do not apply to or in respect of works constructed under this Act.

heading.b: Reservations, dedications and original grants of land

block.txt: A sporting venues authority may manage, develop and otherwise deal with the authority’s land in accordance with this Act despite the terms of any grant, reservation or dedication to which the land is or was subject under any Act or law.
This section is subject to Divisions 2A and 2B.
In this Division—
commencement day means the day on which this Division commences.
Crown land Minister means the Minister administering the Crown Land Management Act 2016.
The scheduled lands continue, on and from the commencement day, to be Crown land dedicated for the purpose of public recreation under the Crown Land Management Act 2016.

heading.b: Venues NSW is Crown land manager of scheduled lands

block.txt: On and from the commencement day—
the appointment of the Sydney Cricket and Sports Ground Trust as Crown land manager for the scheduled lands under the Crown Land Management Act 2016 is taken to be revoked, and
Venues NSW is taken to have been appointed under the Crown Land Management Act 2016 as the Crown land manager for the scheduled lands.
The Crown Land Management Act 2016 applies in relation to the scheduled lands and to Venues NSW in its capacity as the Crown land manager, subject to the following modifications—
Venues NSW’s appointment as the Crown land manager of the scheduled lands cannot be revoked under the Crown Land Management Act 2016,
no other person can be appointed under the Crown Land Management Act 2016 as a Crown land manager of the scheduled lands,
Venues NSW is taken to have been assigned as a category 1 non-council manager of the scheduled lands for the purposes of Division 3.5 of the Crown Land Management Act 2016,
if the Minister is not also the Crown land Minister, the Minister can—

exercise the functions of the Crown land Minister under Part 2 of the Crown Land Management Act 2016 instead of the Crown land Minister in relation to the scheduled lands, except a function prescribed under paragraph (e), and
grant written consent for the purposes of Division 3.5 of the Crown Land Management Act 2016,
the regulations under this Act may prescribe kinds of functions for the purposes of section 3.26(2)(d) of the Crown Land Management Act 2016,
Venues NSW is not required to obtain the Minister’s consent for the exercise of a function prescribed for the purposes of section 3.26(2)(d) of the Crown Land Management Act 2016 or paragraph (e),
the following provisions of the Crown Land Management Act 2016 do not apply in relation to the scheduled lands or Venues NSW—
Division 2.2,
Division 2.4 (except for sections 2.12 and 2.14),
section 2.21,
Division 3.2,
sections 3.14–3.16 and 3.18,
sections 3.29–3.31,
Division 3.6,
section 3.45,
sections 9.12 and 9.25,
Schedule 5,
any other provisions prescribed by the regulations.

If the Minister exercises a function of the Crown land Minister permitted by this section, the exercise of the function has the same effect as if it had been duly exercised by the Crown land Minister.

heading.b: Particular provisions relating to controlled land, designated land and scheduled lands
Carrying out of development on designated land

block.txt: The Minister may approve the following proposals—
the carrying out of development on designated land,
plans or specifications relating to the development.
The Minister’s approval must certify the Minister has consulted the following Ministers in relation to the proposals—
the Minister for the time being administering the Public Works and Procurement Act 1912,
the Minister for the time being administering the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.
This section is repealed at the beginning of the day that is 12 months after the commencement of this section.

heading.b: Application of certain laws to development on designated land

block.txt: The excluded laws do not apply to the following—
the approval of the Minister to the carrying out of development approved by the Minister under section 30AD (the approved development),
the carrying out of the approved development by—
Venues NSW, or
a person on behalf of, or with the authority of, Venues NSW,
the use of the approved development from time to time,
the designated land on which the approved development is carried out or used, or is proposed to be carried out or used.
In this section, excluded laws means—
the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, and
the Local Government Act 1993, and
an instrument in force made under the Acts.

heading.b: Additional uses allowed on scheduled lands

block.txt: Subject to section 30AI, the scheduled lands may be used for purposes permitted on the lands by a State environmental planning policy.
A State environmental planning policy may not permit the use of scheduled lands for a purpose unless the use of the land for the purpose has been approved by the Minister.
Section 30AE does not prevent a provision being included in a State environmental planning policy that applies to designated land.

If a provision included in a State environmental planning policy applies to designated land, section 30AE ceases to apply to the part of the land except in relation to development or use of the land in accordance with an approval under section 30AD—
granted before the day on which the State environmental planning policy took effect, or
granted on or after the day on which the State environmental planning policy took effect in response to an application made by Venues NSW before the day.
This section—
does not affect a provision of a State environmental planning policy in force before the relevant day, and
affects a provision included in a State environmental planning policy after the relevant day only to the extent the provision relates to the scheduled lands.
In this section—
relevant day means the commencement day of the Sydney Cricket and Sports Ground Amendment Act 2006.
State environmental planning policy has the same meaning as in the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

heading.b: Variation or cessation of agreements relating to scheduled lands

block.txt: To enable work to be carried out in relation to the scheduled lands, the Minister may determine an agreement relating to the scheduled lands—
ceases to be binding on a party to the agreement, and
is varied to the extent the Minister deems equitable.
The Minister must not make a determination on an agreement before receiving a report from Venues NSW that recommends the alteration of the agreement.
Notice of the Minister’s determination must be given to the parties to the agreement in writing.
An agreement ceases to have effect or is varied—
in accordance with the terms of the Minister’s notice, and
from the date specified in the Minister’s notice.
In this section—
agreement includes a lease and a licence.

heading.b: Ancillary provisions relating to development and use of scheduled lands for additional purposes

block.txt: The dedication of the scheduled lands for public recreation does not prevent or otherwise affect—
the use of any part of the scheduled lands for a permissible purpose, or
the grant of a lease or licence that permits or otherwise provides for its use for a permissible purpose.
To avoid doubt, a permissible purpose includes a purpose authorised by this Act for the purposes of section 2.12 of the Crown Land Management Act 2016 in its application to the scheduled lands.
In this section, permissible purpose, in relation to a part of the scheduled lands, means a purpose permitted on that part by a State environmental planning policy referred to in section 30AF.

heading.b: Certain uses of Venues NSW’s land restricted

block.txt: Despite any other provision of this Act, any other Act or any instrument made under this or any other Act—
no part of Venues NSW’s land, other than controlled land, may be used for residential accommodation, and
no part of Venues NSW’s land, other than designated land, may be used for tourist and visitor accommodation.
In this section—
residential accommodation means a building or place used predominantly as a place of residence, but does not include tourist and visitor accommodation.
tourist and visitor accommodation means a building or place that provides temporary or short-term accommodation on a commercial basis, and includes hotel accommodation and serviced apartments.

heading.b: No change to dedicated lands except by Act of Parliament

block.txt: The dedication of the scheduled lands cannot be revoked, changed or abolished unless it is done by an Act of Parliament.

heading.b: Transfer of assets, rights and liabilities relating to Stadium Australia
Transfer to Venues NSW of assets, rights and liabilities relating to Stadium Australia

block.txt: The Minister may, by order in writing (a vesting order), transfer assets, rights and liabilities of any of the following persons to Venues NSW—
Stadium Holdings Pty Ltd (ACN 121 891 647),
Stadium Investments Pty Ltd (ACN 121 891 656),
Stadium Australia Management Limited (ACN 069 692 253),

heading.b: No duty payable in relation to agreements, vestings or transfers under Act

states that it is issued under this Act, and

This section does not limit the operation of any other provision of, or made under, this or any other Act relating to proceedings that may be taken in respect of offences.

heading.b: Constitution and procedure of Board of Venues NSW

block.txt: section 15
In this Schedule—
Board means the Board of Venues NSW.
member means a member of the Board and includes a non-GSE member.
non-GSE member means a member of the Board appointed by the Minister under section 15(2)(a), (b) or (d).
Subject to this Schedule and the regulations, a non-GSE member of the Board—
holds office for the term, not exceeding 3 years, specified in the member’s instrument of appointment, and
is eligible, if otherwise qualified, for re-appointment.
A non-GSE member is not eligible to be a member of the Board for consecutive terms totalling more than 9 years.
Non-GSE members hold office as part-time members.

The Minister may, from time to time, determine in consultation with the Secretary of the Premier’s Department an amount of remuneration, including travelling and subsistence allowances, in respect of the office of non-GSE members.
The Minister may—
from time to time, appoint a person to be the deputy of a non-GSE member, and
revoke the appointment at any time.
In the absence of a non-GSE member, the member’s deputy may, if available, act in the place of the member.
While acting in the place of the non-GSE member, a person has all the functions of the member and is taken to be a member.
For the purposes of this clause, a vacancy in the office of a non-GSE member is taken to be an absence of the member.
This clause does not operate to confer on the deputy of a non-GSE member who is the Chairperson the member’s functions as Chairperson.
The office of a member becomes vacant if the member—
dies, or
completes a term of office and is not re-appointed, or
resigns the office by instrument in writing addressed to the Minister, or

is nominated for election as a member of the Legislative Council or of the Legislative Assembly or as a member of a House of Parliament or a legislature of another State or Territory or of the Commonwealth, or

is absent from 3 consecutive meetings of the Board of which reasonable notice has been given to the member personally or by post, except on leave granted by the Minister or unless the member is excused by the Minister for having been absent from the meetings, or

becomes bankrupt, applies to take the benefit of any law for the relief of bankrupt or insolvent debtors, compounds with the member’s creditors or makes an assignment of the member’s remuneration for their benefit, or
becomes a mentally incapacitated person, or

is convicted in New South Wales of an offence that is punishable by imprisonment for 12 months or more or is convicted elsewhere than in New South Wales of an offence that, if committed in New South Wales, would be an offence so punishable, or
is removed from office by the Minister under this clause.
The Minister may remove a member from office at any time.
The Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson vacates office as Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson if they—
are removed from the office by the Minister under this clause, or
resign the office by instrument in writing addressed to the Minister, or
cease to be a member of the Board.
The Minister may remove the Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson from office as Chairperson or Deputy Chairperson at any time.

heading.b: Filling of vacancy in office of member

block.txt: If the office of a member becomes vacant, a person is, subject to this Act and the regulations, to be appointed to fill the vacancy.

heading.b: Casual vacancy in office of non-GSE member

block.txt: A casual vacancy in the office of a non-GSE member is to be filled by a person appointed by the Minister.
The person who fills the casual vacancy holds office, subject to this Act, for the remainder of the term of the member who has vacated office.
In this clause, casual vacancy means a vacancy that occurs other than because of the completion of a term of office.
A member must, as soon as possible after the relevant facts have come to the member’s knowledge, disclose at a meeting of the Board—
that the member has a direct or indirect pecuniary interest in a matter being considered or about to be considered at the meeting, and
the nature of that interest.

A member is not required to disclose an interest under subclause (1) if the interest does not appear to raise a conflict with the proper performance of the member’s duties in relation to consideration of the matter.

One or more of the following disclosures by a member at a meeting of the Board is a sufficient disclosure of the nature of the interest in any matter relating to a specified company or other body or to a specified person that may arise after the date of the disclosure and that is required to be disclosed under subclause (1)—
that the member is a member, or is in the employment, of that company or other body, or
that the member is a partner, or is in the employment, of that person, or
that the member has some other specified interest relating to that company or other body or that person.

Particulars of any disclosure made under this clause must be recorded by the Board in a book kept for the purpose and that book must be open at all reasonable hours for inspection by any person on payment of the fee determined by the Board.
After a member has disclosed the nature of an interest in any matter, the member must not, unless the Minister or the Board otherwise determines—
be present during a deliberation of the Board with respect to the matter, or
take part in any decision of the Board with respect to the matter.
For the purposes of the making of a determination by the Board under subclause (5), a member who has a direct or indirect pecuniary interest in a matter to which the disclosure relates must not—
be present during any deliberation of the Board for the purpose of making the determination, or
take part in the making by the Board of the determination.
A contravention of this clause does not invalidate any decision of the Board.
The provisions of the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 relating to the employment of Public Service employees do not apply to a non-GSE member.

A provision made by or under another Act requiring a person who is the holder of a specified office under that Act to devote the whole of his or her time to the duties of that office, or prohibiting the person from engaging in employment outside the duties of that office, does not operate to disqualify a person from—
holding the specified office and also the office of a member under this Act, or
from accepting and retaining remuneration payable to the person under this Act as a member, if any.
A protected person is not personally subject to any liability for anything done—
in good faith, and
for the purpose of executing functions under this Act.
The liability instead attaches to the Crown.
In this clause—
done includes omitted to be done.
liability means civil liability and includes action, claim or demand.
protected person means—
the Board, or
a member of the Board, or
a person acting under the direction of the Board.
Subject to this Act and the regulations, the Board may call and conduct meetings of the Board as it determines.
The quorum for a Board meeting is a majority of its members for the time being.
The Chairperson presides at a Board meeting.
If the Chairperson is absent from a Board meeting, the Deputy Chairperson presides at the meeting.
If the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson are absent from a Board meeting, another member elected by the members present at the meeting presides at the meeting.
A decision supported by a majority of the votes cast at a Board meeting at which a quorum is present is the decision of the Board.
If there is an equality of votes at a Board meeting, the member presiding at the meeting also has a casting vote.
The Minister may call the first meeting of the Board in the manner that the Chairperson thinks fit.

heading.b: Transaction of business outside meetings or by telephone

block.txt: The Board may, if it thinks fit, transact any of its business by the circulation of papers among all the members of the Board for the time being, and a resolution in writing approved in writing by a majority of the members is taken to be a decision of the Board made at a meeting of the Board.

The Board may, if it thinks fit, transact any of its business at a meeting at which members, or some members, participate by telephone or other electronic means, but only if any member who speaks on a matter before the meeting can be heard by the other members.
The Chairperson and each other member have the same voting rights as they have at an ordinary meeting of the Board for the purposes of—
the approval of a resolution under subclause (1), or
a meeting held in accordance with subclause (2).
A resolution approved under subclause (1) is, subject to the regulations, to be recorded in the minutes of the meetings of the Board.
Papers may be circulated among the members for the purposes of subclause (1) by electronic means.

heading.b: Provisions relating to Chief Executive Officer of Venues NSW

heading.b: Appointment of Chief Executive Officer of Venues NSW

block.txt: The Chief Executive Officer of Venues NSW—
holds office for the term, not exceeding 5 years, specified in the instrument of appointment, and
is eligible, if otherwise qualified, for re-appointment.
A person is not eligible to be a Chief Executive Officer for consecutive terms totalling more than 10 years.
The office of Chief Executive Officer is a full-time office and the holder of the office is required to hold it on that basis.
The employment of the Chief Executive Officer is, subject to this Act and the regulations, to be governed by a contract of employment between the Chief Executive Officer and the Minister.

The office of Chief Executive Officer is a statutory office and the provisions of the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 relating to the employment of Public Service employees do not apply to that office.
The office of Chief Executive Officer becomes vacant if the holder—
dies, or
completes a term of office and is not re-appointed, or
resigns the office by instrument in writing addressed to the Minister, or

is nominated for election as a member of the Legislative Council or of the Legislative Assembly or as a member of a House of Parliament or a legislature of another State or Territory or of the Commonwealth, or

becomes bankrupt, applies to take the benefit of any law for the relief of bankrupt or insolvent debtors, compounds with the Chief Executive Officer’s creditors or makes an assignment of the Chief Executive Officer’s remuneration for their benefit, or
becomes a mentally incapacitated person, or

is convicted in New South Wales of an offence that is punishable by imprisonment for 12 months or more or is convicted elsewhere than in New South Wales of an offence that, if committed in New South Wales, would be an offence so punishable, or
is removed from office under clause 4.
If the office of Chief Executive Officer becomes vacant, a person is, subject to this Act and the regulations, to be appointed to fill the vacancy.
The Minister may, in consultation with the Board of Venues NSW, remove the Chief Executive Officer from office at any time.
The Minister may, from time to time, and in consultation with the Board of Venues NSW, appoint a person to act in the office of Chief Executive Officer during—
the illness or absence of the Chief Executive Officer, or
a vacancy in the office of Chief Executive Officer.
The Minister may remove a person from office as acting Chief Executive Officer at any time.
An acting Chief Executive Officer is entitled to be paid the remuneration, including travelling and subsistence allowances, as the Minister may from time to time determine.

heading.b: Election of members of membership advisory committee by SCG Members

block.txt: section 21E(3)(b)
In this Schedule—
close of nominations date means the date and time fixed by the Returning Officer for the close of nominations for an election.
election means an election, for the purposes of section 21E(3)(b), of persons to be appointed as members of the membership advisory committee constituted under section 21E(1)(a).
Returning Officer means the person appointed by Venues NSW to be the returning officer for an election.
voting SCG Member means a Member of the Sydney Cricket Ground who is of a class prescribed by the regulations.
An election is to be carried out in accordance with this Schedule.
Venues NSW is, by written instrument, to appoint a person as Returning Officer for the purposes of this Schedule.
The Electoral Commissioner for New South Wales (or the Commissioner’s delegate) may, if the Commissioner or delegate consents, be appointed as Returning Officer.
A voting SCG Member is entitled to vote in an election.
Voting in an election is voluntary.
If a voting SCG Member is an organisation, the voting rights of the Member may be exercised by a person authorised by the Member to vote on the Member’s behalf.
If a voting SCG Member is an organisation and holds more than one membership of a class prescribed in the regulations—
the voting SCG Member is entitled to one vote for each membership of the prescribed class held, and
the voting rights attached to each vote are to be exercised by a different person authorised by the voting SCG Member to vote on the voting SCG Member’s behalf.

heading.b: Notice of elections and nomination of candidates

block.txt: As soon as practicable after it has been determined in accordance with this Act that an election is required, Venues NSW is to notify the Returning Officer of the determination.
An election is to be held no more than 90 days after the notification is given.
The Returning Officer is to cause a notice of an election—
to be published in the following—
the Gazette,
at least one newspaper circulating generally throughout New South Wales, whether published in print or on a publicly accessible website,
a prominent place on Venues NSW’s website, and
to be sent by email to all voting SCG Members who have consented to receive notices and other documents relating to their SCG membership by email.
The notice is to—
state that the election is to be held, and
fix the polling day for the election, and
invite nominations from voting SCG Members of candidates to fill the vacancies for elected members of the membership advisory committee, and
fix the close of nominations date, being a date—
at least 21 days after the giving of the notice, and
at least 30 days before the polling day for the election, and
state the Returning Officer’s contact details for the purposes of the lodgment of nominations.
The notice must be given at least 60 days before the polling day for the election.
The Returning Officer may, by means of a further notice of the same kind, fix a later close of nominations date than that fixed by a previous notice for the election.
A nomination of a candidate is to contain the following information—
the full name of the candidate,
the date of birth of the candidate,
the residential address of the candidate,
the membership card number of the candidate,
a statement, signed by the candidate, in which the candidate consents to—
the nomination, and
the use of the information contained in the nomination for the purposes of compiling a candidate information sheet,
the full names, residential addresses, membership card numbers and signatures of at least 6 nominators, being voting SCG Members other than the candidate.
A nomination is to be in writing and may, if the Returning Officer specifies an email address for lodgment of nominations, be in the form of an electronic document sent to the email address.
A nomination is to be lodged with the Returning Officer before the close of nominations date.
A voting SCG Member may nominate no more than 2 candidates in an election.

heading.b: No display of material supporting candidates

block.txt: A person must not post up, exhibit or distribute on the scheduled lands material in support of a candidate’s candidature at an election.
Maximum penalty—1 penalty unit.

If, after the close of nominations date, the number of candidates nominated does not exceed the number of persons required for election, the Returning Officer is to declare the nominated candidates elected.
If, after the close of nominations date, the number of candidates nominated exceeds the number of persons required for election, a poll is to be taken.

If a poll is to be taken, the Chief Executive Officer of Venues NSW, or the Chief Executive Officer’s delegate, is to certify a copy of the roll of all voting SCG Members and provide that copy to the Returning Officer.
The roll is to contain the following information about each voting SCG Member—
the full name of the Member,
the residential address of the Member or other postal address specified by the Member for the purpose of receiving notices and other documents relating to the Member’s SCG membership,
if the Member has consented to receiving notices and other documents relating to the Member’s SCG membership by email—the email address specified for that purpose.
The Returning Officer is to ensure that a copy of the roll is available for inspection free of charge by voting SCG Members.
A voting SCG Member is to notify the Returning Officer of administrative errors relating to the Member’s entry on the roll at least 14 days before the polling day for the election.
If a poll is to be taken, the Returning Officer is to compile a candidate information sheet about each nominated candidate.
The candidate information sheet is to be based on—
information contained in the candidate’s nomination, and
further information voluntarily lodged by the candidate with the Returning Officer before the close of nominations date and intended for inclusion in the candidate information sheet.
Further information referred to in subclause (2)(b) is to be lodged as a statutory declaration in the form of the Eighth Schedule to the Oaths Act 1900, and may include the following—
the name of the candidate’s employer or, if self-employed, the candidate’s present position,
trade, academic or professional qualifications held by the candidate,
organisations of which the candidate is a member,
offices, other than employment, held by the candidate,
additional information relevant to the candidate’s candidature, being no more than 4 typewritten lines.
The Returning Officer may omit or rectify information, or reduce the length of information, from the candidate information sheet that the Returning Officer considers—
is not appropriate for inclusion in a candidate information sheet, or
is misleading in any material particular, or
is of a length greater than the length specified in subclause (3)(e).
The names of the candidates must be listed on the candidate information sheet in the same order as they are listed on the ballot paper for the election.
The ballot paper must contain—
the full names of all candidates nominated for the election, arranged in an order determined by the Returning Officer by drawing lots, and
a box opposite and to the left of the name of each candidate.
If a poll is to be taken, the Returning Officer must provide a voting pack to each voting SCG Member at least 20 days before the polling day for the election.
The voting pack is to be provided—
to a voting SCG Member who has consented to receive notices and other documents relating to the Member’s SCG membership by email—by email to the email address specified for that purpose, and

to any other SCG Member—by post to the Member’s residential address or other postal address specified by the Member for the purpose of receiving notices and other documents relating to the Member’s SCG membership.
A voting pack provided by post is to include the following—
a ballot paper,
a candidate information sheet,
instructions for completing and lodging a ballot paper,
one prepaid envelope addressed to the Returning Officer that contains, on its rear flap, spaces for the insertion of a voting SCG Member’s name, address, signature and membership card number.
A voting pack provided electronically is to include the following—
a ballot paper,
a candidate information sheet,
instructions for completing and lodging a ballot paper.

The Returning Officer may, on written application made by a voting SCG Member, provide a duplicate voting pack to that Member if the Returning Officer is satisfied that the original voting pack has been lost or destroyed.
A voting SCG Member who has received a voting pack may vote by completing and lodging a ballot paper in accordance with the instructions included in the voting pack.
The instructions for completing and lodging a ballot paper are to include the following information—
the polling day for the election,
instructions on how to cast a valid vote by prepaid envelope,
instructions on how to cast a valid vote electronically,
information about the preferential system applicable to the election,
any other information relating to the conduct of the election that the Returning Officer considers appropriate to include.
The instructions on how to cast a valid vote by prepaid envelope are to include the following further information—
instructions on how a voting SCG Member whose voting pack was provided electronically may obtain a prepaid envelope,

a statement that a ballot paper may be lodged, as an alternative to posting the ballot paper, by depositing the ballot paper in a sealed ballot box provided for that purpose at the office of Venues NSW.
The instructions on how to cast a valid vote electronically are to include the following further information—
the internet address of the voting website,
the information, including any applicable password, that a voting SCG Member will require to access the voting website.
The voting website must provide a warning message to a voting SCG Member if there are errors on a ballot paper that the Member attempts to lodge electronically.

If a candidate dies after the close of nominations date and before the polling day, the election is taken to have wholly failed and the Returning Officer is to proceed to give notice of a fresh election in accordance with clause 6.

If a candidate dies on or after the polling day, but before the Returning Officer advises the Chief Executive Officer and the Minister of the result of the election under clause 24, and the candidate—
is not elected—the candidate’s preferences are to be distributed in accordance with clause 22, or
is elected—the candidate who obtained the next highest number of votes is to be declared elected in place of the deceased candidate, or

is elected with the highest number of votes and the election was for the purpose of electing 2 candidates—the candidate who scored the third highest number of votes is to be declared elected in place of the candidate who scored the second highest number of votes.
A candidate may appoint, in writing, a scrutineer to represent that candidate.
Scrutineers may be present during the inspection of prepaid envelopes, the initial scrutiny of ballot papers and the counting of votes.
A candidate may not act as a scrutineer.

The Returning Officer is to ensure that all prepaid envelopes purporting to contain ballot papers that are received before the polling day for an election are stored securely until they are inspected.
On the polling day, the Returning Officer is to inspect each prepaid envelope and reject the envelope if—
the envelope does not have legibly marked on its rear flap the name, address, signature and membership card number that appear to the Returning Officer to be of a voting SCG Member, or
the envelope is not sealed.
On the polling day, the Returning Officer is to—
examine the contents of all prepaid envelopes that were not rejected under clause 19 and all ballot papers that were lodged by deposit in a sealed ballot box in accordance with clause 15(3), and
review all ballot papers that were lodged electronically, and
reject as informal any ballot papers that, in the Returning Officer’s opinion, do not comply with the applicable instructions for casting a valid vote.
Without limiting subclause (1)(c), the Returning Officer is to reject as informal any ballot paper—
in an election for the purpose of electing 2 candidates—if it does not have votes for 2 or more candidates indicated on it, or
in an election for the purpose of electing 1 candidate—if it does not have a vote for 1 or more candidates indicated on it.

If, in the Returning Officer’s opinion, a person’s voting intention is clearly indicated on the voting SCG Member’s ballot paper, the Returning Officer is not to reject the ballot paper merely because the ballot paper contains an unnecessary mark.
The Returning Officer’s determination of the formality or informality of a ballot paper is final.
Following the initial scrutiny carried out under clause 20, the Returning Officer is to—
count the votes recorded for each candidate on all ballot papers that were not rejected as informal in accordance with the preferential system applicable to the election, and
count the informal ballot papers, and
ascertain the results of the count, and
inform the persons present of the result of the count.
Ballot papers are to be counted by the Returning Officer—

in an election for the purpose of electing 2 candidates—according to a multi-preferential system in which preferences 1 and 2 are regarded as primary votes and the remaining recorded preferences, if any, are regarded as secondary votes, or

in an election for the purpose of electing 1 candidate—according to a preferential system in which preference 1 is regarded as a primary vote and the remaining recorded preferences, if any, are regarded as secondary votes.
All preferences recorded on ballot papers are fully transferable.
A determination by the Returning Officer relating to the manner in which an election is to be conducted is final.

heading.b: Election not invalid despite certain omissions

block.txt: An election is not invalid merely because—
a voting SCG Member whose name was on the roll prepared for the election did not receive a voting pack, or
the Returning Officer did not receive a ballot paper lodged by prepaid envelope and sent to the Returning Officer before the polling day for the election.
The Returning Officer is to advise the Chief Executive Officer and the Minister of the result of the election within 7 days after the polling day.

heading.b: Land to be vested in sporting venues authorities

heading.b: Transfer of assets, rights and liabilities of former Trusts

block.txt: In this clause—
transferor, in relation to the transfer of an asset, right or liability by or under this clause, means the former Trust from which the asset, right or liability is transferred.
On the commencement of this clause, the assets, rights or liabilities of a former Trust are transferred to the Hunter Region Sporting Venues Authority.
When any asset, right or liability is transferred by operation of this clause, the following provisions have effect with respect to the transfer—
the rights and liabilities of the transferor become by virtue of this clause the rights and liabilities of the Hunter Region Sporting Venues Authority,

all proceedings relating to the assets, rights or liabilities commenced before the transfer by or on behalf of, or against, the transferor and pending immediately before the transfer are taken to be proceedings pending by or against the Hunter Region Sporting Venues Authority,

any act, matter or thing done or omitted to be done in relation to the assets, rights or liabilities before the transfer by, to or in respect of the transferor is (to the extent to which that act, matter or thing has any force or effect) taken to have been done or omitted by, to or in respect of the Hunter Region Sporting Venues Authority,

a reference in any Act, in any instrument made under any Act or in any document of any kind to the transferor or a predecessor of the transferor is (to the extent that it relates to those assets, rights or liabilities but subject to the regulations), to be read as, or as including, a reference to the Hunter Region Sporting Venues Authority.
The operation of this clause is not to be regarded—
as a breach of contract or confidence or otherwise as a civil wrong, or
as a breach of any contractual provision prohibiting, restricting or regulating the assignment or transfer of assets, rights or liabilities, or

as giving rise to any remedy by a party to an instrument, or as causing or permitting the termination of any instrument, because of a change in the beneficial or legal ownership of any asset, right or liability, or
as an event of default under any contract or other instrument.
No attornment to the transferee by a lessee from a transferor is required.

For all purposes, a former Trust is taken to have had a fee simple, immediately before the commencement of this clause, in land in respect of which it was a reserve trust under the Crown Lands Act 1989 immediately before that commencement.
Subclause (6) has effect despite any provision of the Crown Lands Act 1989 and, in particular, section 100 of that Act.
The Minister may, by notice in writing, confirm a transfer of particular assets, rights or liabilities by operation of this Part.

Land of a former Trust transferred by operation of this Act is transferred free of any reservation, grant or dedication to which the land was subject under any Act or law.

heading.b: Authorised persons under Sydney Cricket Ground and Sydney Football Stadium By-law 2014

block.txt: A person who was authorised by the Sydney Cricket and Sports Ground Trust for a function referred to in Part 6 or 7 the Sydney Cricket Ground and Sydney Football Stadium By-law 2014 immediately before its repeal is taken, on and from the repeal day, to have been appointed as a ranger under section 37 of this Act.

heading.b: References to dissolved, abolished or reconstituted bodies or offices

block.txt: Unless the regulations provide differently, a reference in any instrument to any of the following is, on and from the repeal day, to be read as including a reference to reconstituted Venues NSW—
the Sydney Cricket and Sports Ground Trust,
existing Venues NSW,
a Local Venues Council.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to how references in instruments to bodies or offices dissolved, abolished or reconstituted by this Part should be read.
